approvalTitle: New Document dialog, units, recent files: requirements
content:
# Requirements Document

## Introduction

Today PressToShape starts with a fixed 600 × 400 px document, File → New silently creates the same, and a document's size can't be chosen or expressed in real-world units.

This spec adds a **New Document dialog**, the first thing users see:
- it opens over the main window at startup;
- it opens on every File → New.

It offers:
- **presets** by purpose (print, screen, web, icons);
- **custom dimensions in real units** (px, mm, cm, in, pt) with **DPI**;
- orientation;
- at startup, also **Open…** and a list of **recent files**, plus a way to **not show it at startup**.

To make print sizes like A4 meaningful, documents get **units and DPI**:
- a document remembers its unit and resolution;
- the panels show sizes and positions in that unit;
- `.p2s` and SVG files keep the real size;
- PNG export can use the document's DPI.

Recent files also get their own menu, File → Open Recent.

## Alignment with Product Vision

- **Feature gap list, P1 "Document and app"**: document properties with presets (A4, Letter, 1080p, …) and recent files; **P1 "Layout and precision"**: units px / mm / cm / in / pt, document size in units, DPI.
- **Target users**: graphic designers making print and screen work need real sizes; people leaving Illustrator or Affinity expect a new-document dialog with presets and units.
- **Principle 2, Professional depth, approachable surface**: the dialog makes the first decision explicit and quick (one click on a preset), while units and DPI are there when needed.
- **Principle 5, Inkscape interop**: SVG files carry their real size (e.g. `width="210mm"`), so an A4 drawing opens as A4 in Inkscape and the other way round.
- **Reliability**: format change with version bump and migration, as the native format rules require.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1: New Document dialog at startup and on New

**User Story:** As an artist, I want to decide what I'm making when I start, so that my canvas has the right size from the beginning.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN PressToShape starts without a file to open THEN the main window SHALL open as usual (restored size and position) and the New Document dialog SHALL open on top of it, modal.
2. WHEN the user chooses File → New THEN the same dialog SHALL open (without the startup-only parts, see Requirement 4).
3. WHEN the user confirms the dialog (Create, Enter, or double-click on a preset) THEN a new empty document with the chosen size, unit and DPI SHALL replace the current one. The view SHALL fit the artboard into the window.
4. IF the current document has unsaved changes AND the user confirms the dialog THEN the existing "Save changes?" question SHALL appear first. Cancel there SHALL keep the current document and close nothing else.
5. WHEN the user cancels the dialog at startup (Cancel, Esc, window close button) THEN the default document SHALL be created: the last used settings, or the built-in default on first start.
6. WHEN the user cancels the dialog opened by File → New THEN nothing SHALL change.
7. Creating a document SHALL NOT be an undo step, and the new document SHALL NOT be marked dirty (as New today).

### Requirement 2: Presets

**User Story:** As a designer, I want common formats one click away, so that I don't have to look up dimensions.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The dialog SHALL list presets grouped by category, each showing its name and size in its own unit. The first version SHALL have at least:
   - **Print**: A3, A4, A5, A6 (mm), US Letter, US Legal, Tabloid (in), business card 85 × 55 mm. Default DPI 300.
   - **Screen**: HD 1280 × 720, Full HD 1920 × 1080, QHD 2560 × 1440, 4K UHD 3840 × 2160 (px). Default DPI 96.
   - **Web and social**: Square post 1080 × 1080, Portrait post 1080 × 1350, Story 1080 × 1920, Link preview 1200 × 630 (px).
   - **Icons**: 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 px squares.
2. WHEN a preset is selected THEN the size, unit, DPI and orientation fields SHALL show its values. Editing any field afterwards SHALL mark the choice as "Custom" without changing the preset itself.
3. Preset and category names SHALL be translatable; dimensions are not.
4. The selection of the last created document SHALL be preselected the next time (preset, or custom values).

### Requirement 3: Custom size, units, DPI and orientation

**User Story:** As a designer, I want to enter exact dimensions in the unit I think in, so that my document matches the target format.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The dialog SHALL have fields for:
   - width and height;
   - unit: px, mm, cm, in, pt;
   - DPI;
   - orientation: portrait / landscape, by buttons that swap width and height.
2. WHEN the unit changes THEN width and height SHALL be converted so the physical size stays the same (210 mm → 8.27 in). DPI SHALL be used to convert from and to px.
3. WHEN the DPI changes AND the unit is a physical one (mm, cm, in, pt) THEN the physical size SHALL stay and only the pixel equivalent changes. WHEN the unit is px THEN the pixel size SHALL stay.
4. The dialog SHALL show the resulting size in the other system as a hint ("2480 × 3508 px" for A4 at 300 DPI; "210 × 297 mm" for px documents with a DPI).
5. Width and height SHALL have sane limits:
   - at least 1 px;
   - at most a size whose pixel equivalent fits the renderer's limits.

   Invalid input SHALL disable Create with a short reason, never produce a broken document.
6. Numbers SHALL use the interface language's number format (decimal comma in German), as all number fields do.

### Requirement 4: Startup choices

**User Story:** As a returning user, I want to continue my recent work right from the start, or skip the dialog when I always start the same way.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. At startup the dialog SHALL also show:
   - an **Open…** button;
   - a list of **recent files** (name, folder, last opened), most recent first.
2. WHEN the user picks Open… THEN the regular open dialog SHALL appear, and on success the file opens instead of a new document. Cancelling that open dialog SHALL return to the New Document dialog.
3. WHEN the user activates a recent file (double-click or Enter) THEN it SHALL open. IF the file no longer exists or can't be read THEN the dialog SHALL stay open, show the reason, and offer to remove the entry from the list.
4. The dialog SHALL have a **"Show at startup"** checkbox (on by default). The same setting SHALL be in Settings, in a new **General** category.
5. WHEN "Show at startup" is off THEN PressToShape SHALL start with the default document (Requirement 1.5) without the dialog. File → New SHALL still show the dialog.
6. WHEN PressToShape is started with a file to open (e.g. from the command line or a file manager, where supported) THEN the dialog SHALL NOT appear and the file SHALL open.

### Requirement 5: Recent files

**User Story:** As a user, I want quick access to files I worked on recently, also when the startup dialog isn't shown.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every successfully opened or saved file (`.p2s` or SVG) SHALL move to the top of the recent files list. The list SHALL hold at most 10 files and be stored with the app settings.
2. File → **Open Recent** SHALL list the same files (numbered, with their name), plus **Clear Recent Files**. An empty list SHALL show a disabled "No recent files" entry.
3. WHEN a recent entry no longer exists THEN opening it SHALL show the reason in the status bar and remove it from the list.
4. Opening a recent file SHALL ask about unsaved changes first, as Open does.
5. The portable build SHALL keep the list in its `settings.ini`, like other settings.

### Requirement 6: Units in the document

**User Story:** As a designer, I want to see and enter positions and sizes in my document's unit, so that I don't have to convert in my head.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every document SHALL have a **unit** and a **DPI**. Existing documents, SVG files without units and new documents from px presets SHALL use px at 96 DPI, so their behaviour is unchanged.
2. The selection panel's X, Y, W, H, centre, radius and stroke width fields SHALL show and accept values in the document's unit, with sensible decimals per unit (px 2, mm 2, cm 3, in 3, pt 2).
3. The drawing SHALL NOT change when values are only displayed in another unit. Changing a document's unit after creation is out of scope (document properties come later).
4. Font size SHALL stay in pt, as type is measured in most design tools.
5. Zoom 100% SHALL show one document pixel per screen pixel, as today. For a 300 DPI A4 document that means 100% is large, and Zoom to Fit is the usual view: a new document SHALL open fitted (Requirement 1.3).

### Requirement 7: Files keep the real size

**User Story:** As a user exchanging files, I want an A4 drawing to stay A4 in other programs.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. `.p2s` files SHALL store the document's unit and DPI. This changes the stored format, so the format version SHALL increase to 2 with a migration from version 1 (px, 96 DPI) and a version 2 sample file, following the format rules (`docs/file-format.md`).
2. SVG export SHALL write width and height in the document's unit (e.g. `width="210mm" height="297mm"`) with a `viewBox` in document coordinates, so other programs show the real size and the drawing is unchanged.
3. SVG import SHALL read `width`/`height` units (px, mm, cm, in, pt, pc) and set the document's unit and DPI accordingly. Documents without units stay px at 96 DPI.
4. A file saved by PressToShape and opened in Inkscape SHALL show the same physical page size; an Inkscape A4 file SHALL open as A4 in mm.

### Requirement 8: PNG export uses DPI

**User Story:** As a designer, I want to export a print document at its resolution without calculating a scale.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The Export PNG dialog SHALL offer DPI next to scale: entering one updates the other, and the resulting pixel size is shown (as today).
2. The default SHALL be the document's DPI (scale 1 for px documents, as today).
3. The exported PNG SHALL record its DPI in the file (pHYs), so print tools pick up the physical size.

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Code Architecture and Modularity
- **Unit math** (conversions between px, mm, cm, in, pt for a DPI, rounding per unit) is pure, Qt-free and tested, in `geometry/` or `models/`.
- **Presets** are data (a table of name, category, size, unit, DPI), not code in the dialog. Adding a preset is one line.
- **Recent files** and "show at startup" are app settings behind typed accessors in `views/app_settings.py`; the list logic (move to top, limit, remove missing) is plain Python and tested.
- Creating a document from the dialog goes through one operation (`documents.new_document` with size, unit, DPI). The dialog only collects values.
- **The Settings window** gets a General page through the existing page mechanism.

### Performance
- The dialog SHALL appear within the usual startup time; the recent files list SHALL NOT read the files, only check that they exist.

### Reliability
- Round-trip tests for unit and DPI through `.p2s` and SVG.
- Migration test with the version 1 sample.
- Unit conversion tests (A4 at 72, 96, 300 DPI; inches ↔ mm ↔ pt).
- A test that existing px documents behave exactly as before.

### Usability
- Keyboard: the preset list has focus; arrow keys move, Enter creates, Esc cancels. No shortcut beyond the dialog's own keys (CLAUDE.md shortcut rule).
- All texts translatable; German translation complete.
- Out of scope:
  - changing size, unit or DPI of an existing document (Document Properties, a later spec);
  - artboard background colour;
  - multiple artboards;
  - user-defined presets;
  - rulers and grids in units;
  - templates (documents as starting points);
  - thumbnails of recent files;
  - opening files from the command line, if not already supported.
